data.title: Middle East Eye: As the US pulls its forces out of Iraq, what happens to Iran-backed armed groups?
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
As the US pulls its forces out of Iraq, what happens to Iran-backed armed groups?
The US has announced the withdrawal of its forces from Iraq, 23 years after the invasion that overthrew Saddam Hussein.
The development has been hailed by the Iraqi government as a final return to "national sovereignty" after years of American involvement in the country.
"October 1 will be a new day in the course of the Iraqi state, with the country free of any foreign military presence and the completion of national sovereignty over its territory," Iraq's Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said in a statement.
His statement is not quite accurate - Turkey still maintains a military presence in the country, though it has also pledged to soon hand over its Bashiqa-Zilkan military base in northern Iraq to the government.
The end of the US presence in Iraq, the deadline for which was 30 September, had originally also been tied to the disarming of the extra-government armed groups that, since the overthrow of Saddam, have been among the most powerful forces in the country.

data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Qatar criticises Israeli ‘breaches of international law’ in Palestine, Lebanon and Syria
Qatar has called Israeli attacks on Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, as well as Syria and Lebanon, "grave violations of international law", according to a statement from the country's Permanent Representative of the State of Qatar to the United Nations Office in Geneva, Dr Hend Abdulrahman al-Muftah.
"The State of Qatar affirmed that the continued Israeli occupation, grave violations and crimes against Palestinians, illegal settlement expansion, attempts to forcibly displace Palestinians, and attacks on Syria and Lebanon constitute grave violations of international law," Qatar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs wrote in a post on X on Tuesday.
The statement added that Israel's refusal to implement the plan to end the conflict in Gaza "represents a direct challenge and a deliberate attempt to undermine international efforts aimed at achieving a just, comprehensive, and lasting peace" and called on the international community "to shoulder its responsibilities to end the Israeli occupation".

data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
US to release 40 million barrels of crude from Strategic Petroleum Reserve
The US energy department said on Tuesday it is offering to loan energy companies 40 million barrels of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR), in an effort to control soaring fuel prices ahead of the US midterm elections.
The US agreed in March to loan 172 million barrels of oil from the SPR as part of a wider deal with about 30 countries in the International Energy Agency (IEA) to release 400 million barrels.
In June, the Trump administration offered to loan the last 40 million barrels from that IEA agreement, but revealed later that month that companies only agreed to borrow about 500,000 barrels.

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband speaks at the annual Labour Party conference in Liverpool, on 28 September 2026 (Oli Scarff/AFP)
Off
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband’s words, in his speech to the Labour Party conference in Liverpool on Monday, were striking.
Gaza is a “stain on the conscience of the world”, he said, adding that those who protested at the Labour government’s support for Israel “were right”.
Clearly, this is a significant rhetorical departure from the Starmer era, when Labour had to be dragged kicking and screaming into making even the most tepid criticisms of Israel.
In his address to conference delegates, Miliband took aim at “ethnic cleansing by the settler terrorists” in the occupied West Bank, along with “war crimes” in Gaza and Israel’s “illegal occupation of Palestine”. He vowed to “match words with actions”.
This last point is crucial: talk is cheap. What really matters is how far this new language reflects any real corresponding policy shift.
Miliband’s recent announcement of sanctions on West Bank settlements was a start, but it did not fundamentally alter the UK’s relationship with Israel; UK diplomats assured the White House that the sanctions were primarily “symbolic”.
By the same token, Miliband’s speech, for all its headline-grabbing rhetoric, largely avoided confronting the structures and alliances that make Britain complicit in Israeli genocide and settler-colonialism.

French far-right Rassemblement National party president Jordan Bardella poses during a photo session in Paris, on 31 January 2024 (Joel Saget/AFP)
Off
Mediapart plunged the French far right into chaos on Monday after reporting that Jordan Bardella, president of the National Rally (RN) party, had made antisemitic comments in private messages.
Bardella, 31, was fighting for his political career on Tuesday after the investigative outlet obtained exchanges dating from 2013 to 2015.
According to Mediapart, the messages show Bardella promoting conspiracy theories about Jews, banks, the French government, and a supposed “new world order dominated by Israel”.
Bardella was 17 years old when the earliest exchanges reportedly took place and had recently joined the party under far-right leader Marine Le Pen.
Bardella denied making the comments and described the reports as part of a “total war” to derail Le Pen’s 2027 presidential campaign.
Mediapart described him as having an “obsession with the supposed Judeo-Zionist control of the country”.
The outlet said it had authenticated the private exchanges but had not publicly released the messages.
In messages cited by Mediapart, Bardella allegedly wrote that “all banks are owned by Jews” and that “the Jew must dominate other peoples, crush them and rob them; a Zionist is necessarily Jewish, and profoundly Jewish. In France, two clear examples are BHL (Bernard-Henri Levy) or (Jacques) Attali. And that is what they want, a New World Order dominated by Israel, with Jerusalem, of course, as its capital.”

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland is pictured during the Fifa Club World Cup 2025 round of 16 football match between his team and Saudi Arabia's Al Hilal, at the Camping World stadium in Orlando, Florida, on 30 June 2025 (Patricia De Melo/AFP)
Off
An independent commission on Tuesday revealed that Manchester City Football Club has been found guilty on all 115 charges related to financial rules violations since 2009.
The club engaged in "sham" commercial contracts to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than $1bn, the findings showed.
"The Club’s financial statements had not been prepared and audited in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory principles," the commission wrote.
It was "reckless" and "acted other than with utmost good faith", it added.
In a video sent to staff and players and obtained by Sky Sports News, City's chief executive, Ferran Soriano, called the investigation a "Premier League conspiracy theory".
The Premier League charged City in 2023 after an investigation into alleged breaches between 2009 and 2018.
It was accused of failing to provide accurate financial information and details of payments to players and coaches, as well as breaches of financial sustainability rules.
“This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in [our] history," the Premier League said in a statement on Tuesday.
"[It] vindicates the Premier League’s decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently," the statement added.

Saudi Arabia appears to be mending fences with the UAE in an effort to push back a Houthi military offensive in Yemen that threatens the kingdom’s Red Sea oil export corridor and has seen drones strike Riyadh.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman hosted UAE Vice President Mansour bin Zayed in Riyadh on Tuesday, marking the kingdom's most prominent effort yet to reconcile with the UAE after clashing over Sudan, Yemen, and Somaliland.
“The Houthis are bringing Saudi Arabia and the UAE closer together,” Anna Jacobs, a non-resident fellow at the Arab Gulf States Institute, told Middle East Eye.
The two neighbours have been discussing how to collaborate on Yemen for months, western and Arab officials tell MEE, but the talks have been moving slowly.
The UAE wanted a public signal from Saudi Arabia that it had put its spat behind it, along with concessions to Abu Dhabi’s allies on the ground in Yemen, the western official told MEE. In July, Saudi Arabia shared a casual photograph of Mansour and Saudi Defence Minister Khaled bin Salman together, but the location and time of the meeting were not disclosed.
The Houthis' lightning offensive in September down the Red Sea coast was the catalyst for a bigger meeting, experts say.
Mansour, the brother of UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed, was greeted at the airport by Khaled bin Salman, the crown prince’s brother, whom MEE revealed was tapped by the crown prince in February to mend the rift.

data.summary:
Trump says he does not know if Iran is going to 'give up yet'
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that Iran is doing "very poorly," adding that he does not know if Iran is going to "give up yet" in its war with the US, in comments delivered to reporters outside the White House following a meeting with AI executives.

data.title: Middle East Eye: IRGC issues open letter urging US voters to 'wrest control back from corrupt politicians'
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
IRGC issues open letter urging US voters to 'wrest control back from corrupt politicians'
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) released on Tuesday an open letter addressed to US voters, calling on them to "wake up" and "wrest control back from corrupt politicians".
In a lengthy open letter, the IRGC directly appealed to American voters, telling them, "you are the ones who empower, with your votes, the government and allow it to do what it does".
"The United States of America is a great nation. To allow vulgar and immoral individuals to continue steering your politics and policies will only further humiliate and undermine the US," the letter continued, urging the American public to "take back control".
This comes ahead of the US midterm elections at a time when Trump's popularity is at an all-time low.
